      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	"""Persistent execution plans over ``dispatch`` claims.
2	
3	One on-disk document (version 1), the execution ledger, holds the whole
4	execution layer on top of the dispatch ledger:
5	
6	* ``plans`` maps each job id to its execution plans keyed by the
7	  dispatch attempt number, each plan binding the traded resource
8	  version, the job deadline, the claiming owner and the lease end, with
9	  a kind (``launch`` or ``migrate``), an optional source resource, a
10	  lifecycle state (``active``, ``completed``, ``failed`` or
11	  ``interrupted``) and the step receipts recorded so far;
12	* ``idempotency`` binds each call key to the complete request it first
13	  served (action, job id and moment, plus owner, source, attempt, step,
14	  result or receipt where the action carries them);
15	* ``audit`` holds one event per first-served key, binding the complete
16	  request and the plan snapshot the call committed.
17	
18	:func:`plan` reads the ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file, the resource
19	supply file, the ``market.clear`` clearing ledger and the dispatch
20	ledger as one snapshot under their shared locks together with the
21	execution ledger's exclusive lock, all five taken in resolved real-path
22	order, and creates the plan for one claimed decision: numbered by the
23	dispatch attempt count, it fixes the job, the target resource version,
24	the deadline, the owner and the lease end. An empty source yields a
25	``launch`` plan (steps ``stage`` then ``start``); a non-empty source
26	yields a ``migrate`` plan (steps ``copy`` then ``switch``) and must
27	name a published resource other than the target whose residency covers
28	the job's. :func:`record` and :func:`recover` only touch the execution
29	ledger under its exclusive lock: recording appends one step receipt --
30	steps advance only on success, any failure terminates the plan as
31	``failed`` and a successful last step as ``completed`` -- and recovering
32	turns a plan whose lease has strictly expired into ``interrupted`` with
33	every receipt preserved. The execution ledger is created only by the
34	first plan; every other call facing a missing ledger fails with
35	``FileNotFoundError``.
36	
37	Every read requires the on-disk bytes to be exactly the canonical
38	compact form :func:`_canonical_bytes` produces -- sections in their
39	fixed order, primary keys sorted by code point, compact UTF-8 JSON with
40	non-ASCII written through, no negative-zero or non-finite number

182	        raise ValueError("plan source must differ from its target")
183	    version = record["version"]
184	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version < 1:
185	        raise ValueError("plan version must be a positive integer")
186	    deadline = record["deadline"]
187	    if not _is_plain_int(deadline) or deadline < 0:
188	        raise ValueError("plan deadline must be a non-boolean "
189	                         "non-negative integer")
190	    owner = record["owner"]
191	    if not isinstance(owner, str) or not owner:
192	        raise ValueError("plan owner must be a non-empty string")
193	    lease_end = record["lease_end"]
194	    if not _is_plain_int(lease_end) or lease_end < 1:
195	        raise ValueError("plan lease_end must be a positive integer")
196	    if lease_end > deadline:
197	        raise ValueError("plan lease end must not pass the job deadline")
198	    state = record["state"]
199	    if state not in _STATES:
200	        raise ValueError("plan state is invalid")
201	
202	    sequence = _STEPS[kind]
203	    steps_raw = record["steps"]
204	    if not isinstance(steps_raw, list) or len(steps_raw) > len(sequence):
205	        raise ValueError("plan steps must be a list within the step "
206	                         "sequence")
207	    steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
208	    for index, receipt_raw in enumerate(steps_raw):
209	        steps.append(_validate_receipt(receipt_raw, sequence, index,
210	                                       lease_end))
211	
212	    # The state must be exactly what the recorded receipts imply: a
213	    # failed receipt terminates the plan and must be the last one, a
214	    # complete successful sequence terminates it as completed, and
215	    # anything else is active or recovered-interrupted.
216	    failed = [receipt for receipt in steps if receipt["result"] == "failed"]
217	    if failed:
218	        if steps[-1]["result"] != "failed" or len(failed) != 1:
219	            raise ValueError("a failed step must terminate the plan")
220	        if state != "failed":
221	            raise ValueError("a plan with a failed step must be failed")
222	    elif len(steps) == len(sequence):
223	        if state != "completed":
224	            raise ValueError("a fully recorded plan must be completed")
225	    elif state not in ("active", "interrupted"):
226	        raise ValueError("an unfinished plan must be active or "
227	                         "interrupted")
228	
229	    return {
230	        "job_id": job_id,
231	        "attempt": attempt,
232	        "kind": kind,
233	        "source": source,
234	        "resource_id": resource_id,
235	        "version": version,
236	        "deadline": deadline,
237	        "owner": owner,
238	        "lease_end": lease_end,
239	        "state": state,
240	        "steps": steps,
241	    }

244	def _validate_request(request: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
245	    if not isinstance(request, dict):
246	        raise ValueError("request must be an object")
247	    action = request.get("action")
248	    if not isinstance(action, str) or action not in _REQUEST_FIELDS:
249	        raise ValueError("request action is invalid")
250	    if set(request.keys()) != set(_REQUEST_FIELDS[action]):
251	        raise ValueError("request has invalid fields")
252	    job_id = request["job_id"]
253	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
254	        raise ValueError("request job_id must be a non-empty string")
255	    at = request["at"]
256	    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
257	        raise ValueError("request at must be a non-boolean non-negative "
258	                         "integer")
259	    normalized: dict[str, Any] = {"action": action, "job_id": job_id}
260	    if action in ("record", "recover"):
261	        attempt = request["attempt"]
262	        if not _is_plain_int(attempt) or attempt < 1:
263	            raise ValueError("request attempt must be a positive integer")
264	        normalized["attempt"] = attempt
265	    if action in ("plan", "record"):
266	        owner = request["owner"]
267	        if not isinstance(owner, str) or not owner:
268	            raise ValueError("request owner must be a non-empty string")
269	        normalized["owner"] = owner
270	    if action == "plan":
271	        source = request["source"]
272	        if source is not None \
273	                and (not isinstance(source, str) or not source):
274	            raise ValueError("request source must be null or a non-empty "
275	                             "string")
276	        normalized["source"] = source
277	    if action == "record":
278	        step = request["step"]
279	        if step not in _ALL_STEPS:
280	            raise ValueError("request step is invalid")
281	        normalized["step"] = step
282	        result = request["result"]
283	        if result not in _RESULTS:
284	            raise ValueError("request result is invalid")
285	        normalized["result"] = result
286	        receipt = request["receipt"]
287	        if not isinstance(receipt, str) or not receipt:
288	            raise ValueError("request receipt must be a non-empty string")
289	        normalized["receipt"] = receipt
290	    normalized["at"] = at
291	    return {field: normalized[field] for field in _REQUEST_FIELDS[action]}

294	def _validate_ledger(
295	    data: object,
296	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
297	           dict[str, dict[str, Any]]]:
298	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
299	        raise ValueError("execution ledger root must be an object with "
300	                         "keys version, plans, idempotency and audit")
301	    version = data["version"]
302	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
303	        raise ValueError("unsupported execution ledger version")
304	
305	    plans_raw = data["plans"]
306	    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
307	    audit_raw = data["audit"]
308	    if not isinstance(plans_raw, dict) \
309	            or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict) \
310	            or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
311	        raise ValueError("plans, idempotency and audit must be objects")
312	    _check_sorted_keys(plans_raw, "plans")
313	    _check_sorted_keys(idempotency_raw, "idempotency")
314	    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")
315	
316	    plans: dict[str, dict[str, dict[str, Any]]] = {}
317	    for job_id, attempts_raw in plans_raw.items():
318	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
319	            raise ValueError("plan job ids must be non-empty strings")
320	        if not isinstance(attempts_raw, dict) or not attempts_raw:
321	            raise ValueError("plans must hold a non-empty attempt map "
322	                             "per job")
323	        _check_sorted_keys(attempts_raw, "plans")
324	        attempts: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
325	        for attempt_key, record in attempts_raw.items():
326	            plan = _validate_plan(record)
327	            if plan["job_id"] != job_id:
328	                raise ValueError("plan record id does not match its key")
329	            if not isinstance(attempt_key, str) \
330	                    or str(plan["attempt"]) != attempt_key:
331	                raise ValueError("plan record attempt does not match its "
332	                                 "key")
333	            attempts[attempt_key] = plan
334	        plans[job_id] = attempts
335	
336	    idempotency: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
337	    for key, request_raw in idempotency_raw.items():
338	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
339	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
340	        idempotency[key] = _validate_request(request_raw)
341	
342	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
343	    for key, event_raw in audit_raw.items():
344	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
345	            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
346	        if not isinstance(event_raw, dict) \
347	                or set(event_raw.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
348	            raise ValueError("execution audit event has invalid fields")
349	        if event_raw["key"] != key or not isinstance(event_raw["key"], str):
350	            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
351	        request = _validate_request(event_raw["request"])
352	        result = _validate_plan(event_raw["result"])
353	        if request["job_id"] != result["job_id"]:
354	            raise ValueError("audit event result does not match its "
355	                             "request")
356	        events[key] = {"key": key, "request": request, "result": result}
357	
358	    # The three sections describe one execution history: each
359	    # idempotency key binds one request and one event, and the event
360	    # carries exactly the bound request.
361	    if set(idempotency) != set(events):
362	        raise ValueError("idempotency keys and audit events do not match")
363	    for key, request in idempotency.items():
364	        if events[key]["request"] != request:
365	            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its idempotency "
366	                             "entry")
367	
368	    # A plan's job id, attempt, kind, source, target resource version,
369	    # deadline, owner and lease end never change after the plan is
370	    # created; every recorded result snapshot must agree with them.
371	    fixed = ("job_id", "attempt", "kind", "source", "resource_id",
372	             "version", "deadline", "owner", "lease_end")
373	    creations: dict[tuple[str, int], str] = {}
374	    recordings: dict[tuple[str, int], list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
375	    recoveries: dict[tuple[str, int], int] = {}
376	    for key, request in idempotency.items():
377	        result = events[key]["result"]
378	        slot = (result["job_id"], result["attempt"])
379	        attempts = plans.get(result["job_id"])
380	        current = attempts.get(str(result["attempt"])) \
381	            if attempts is not None else None
382	        if current is None:
383	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a recorded plan")
384	        for field in fixed:
385	            if result[field] != current[field]:
386	                raise ValueError("audit event result does not match its "
387	                                 "plan")
388	        action = request["action"]
389	        if action == "plan":
390	            if slot in creations:
391	                raise ValueError("attempt planned under more than one "
392	                                 "idempotency key")
393	            creations[slot] = key
394	            if result["state"] != "active" or result["steps"] != []:
395	                raise ValueError("plan audit result must be a fresh "
396	                                 "active plan")
397	            if request["owner"] != result["owner"] \
398	                    or request["source"] != result["source"]:
399	                raise ValueError("plan audit result does not match its "
400	                                 "request")
401	            if request["at"] > result["lease_end"]:
402	                raise ValueError("plan request must lie inside the lease")
403	        elif action == "record":
404	            if request["attempt"] != result["attempt"]:
405	                raise ValueError("record audit result does not match its "
406	                                 "request")
407	            if not result["steps"]:
408	                raise ValueError("record audit result must carry the "
409	                                 "recorded step")
410	            receipt = result["steps"][-1]
411	            if receipt != {"step": request["step"],
412	                           "result": request["result"],
413	                           "receipt": request["receipt"],
414	                           "at": request["at"]}:
415	                raise ValueError("record audit result does not match its "
416	                                 "request")
417	            recordings.setdefault(slot, []).append(receipt)
418	        else:  # recover
419	            if request["attempt"] != result["attempt"]:
420	                raise ValueError("recover audit result does not match "
421	                                 "its request")
422	            if result["state"] != "interrupted":
423	                raise ValueError("recover audit result must be an "
424	                                 "interrupted plan")
425	            if request["at"] <= result["lease_end"]:
426	                raise ValueError("recover request must lie past the "
427	                                 "lease end")
428	            recoveries[slot] = recoveries.get(slot, 0) + 1
429	
430	    if set(creations) != {(job_id, plan["attempt"])
431	                          for job_id, attempts in plans.items()
432	                          for plan in attempts.values()}:
433	        raise ValueError("every plan must be bound to a plan request")
434	
435	    # The recorded steps of a plan are exactly the receipts its record
436	    # requests committed, and an interrupted plan is exactly one whose
437	    # recovery was recorded.
438	    for job_id, attempts in plans.items():
439	        for plan in attempts.values():
440	            slot = (job_id, plan["attempt"])
441	            committed = sorted(json.dumps(receipt, sort_keys=True)
442	                               for receipt in recordings.get(slot, []))
443	            held = sorted(json.dumps(receipt, sort_keys=True)
444	                          for receipt in plan["steps"])
445	            if committed != held:
446	                raise ValueError("plan steps do not match the record "
447	                                 "history")
448	            if (plan["state"] == "interrupted") \
449	                    != (recoveries.get(slot, 0) == 1):
450	                raise ValueError("plan state does not match the recover "
451	                                 "history")
452	            if recoveries.get(slot, 0) > 1:
453	                raise ValueError("plan recovered more than once")
454	
455	    return plans, idempotency, events

458	def _canonical_bytes(
459	    plans: dict[str, dict[str, dict[str, Any]]],
460	    idempotency: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
461	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
462	) -> bytes:
463	    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, sections in their
464	    # fixed field order and each section's primary keys in code-point
465	    # order, terminated by exactly one newline.
466	    payload = {
467	        "version": _VERSION,
468	        "plans": {job_id: {attempt: plans[job_id][attempt]
469	                           for attempt in sorted(plans[job_id])}
470	                  for job_id in sorted(plans)},
471	        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
472	        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
473	    }
474	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
475	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
476	    return text.encode("utf-8")

479	def _load_ledger(
480	    realpath: str,
481	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
482	           dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None]:
483	    try:
484	        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
485	            raw = handle.read()
486	    except FileNotFoundError:
487	        return {}, {}, {}, None
488	    try:
489	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
490	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
491	        raise ValueError(
492	            f"execution ledger {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
493	    try:
494	        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
495	        data = finite_loads(text)
496	    except ValueError as exc:
497	        raise ValueError(
498	            f"execution ledger {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
499	    plans, idempotency, events = _validate_ledger(data)
500	    # As for the other registries, the ledger is accepted only in
501	    # canonical compact form with a single trailing newline.
502	    if raw != _canonical_bytes(plans, idempotency, events):
503	        raise ValueError(
504	            f"execution ledger {realpath!r} is not in canonical compact "
505	            "form")
506	    return plans, idempotency, events, raw

517	def _rollback_file(realpath: str, directory: str, old_bytes: bytes | None,
518	                   first: BaseException) -> None:
519	    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held,
520	    # or remove a ledger that did not exist beforehand, then sync the
521	    # directory. A failed recovery chains after the original error.
522	    try:
523	        if old_bytes is None:
524	            try:
525	                os.unlink(realpath)
526	            except FileNotFoundError:
527	                pass
528	        else:
529	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
530	                dir=directory, prefix=".execution-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
531	            try:
532	                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
533	                    handle.write(old_bytes)
534	                    handle.flush()
535	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
536	                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
537	            except BaseException:
538	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
539	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
540	                raise
541	        _fsync_directory(directory)
542	    except OSError as recovery:
543	        raise recovery from first

546	def _commit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
547	                 old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
548	    # One durable commit for the plan, the idempotency binding and the
549	    # audit event: synced same-directory temporary, atomic replace and a
550	    # directory fsync, restoring the pre-call bytes on any failure.
551	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
552	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
553	        dir=directory, prefix=".execution-", suffix=".tmp")
554	    try:
555	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
556	            handle.write(payload)
557	            handle.flush()
558	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
559	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
560	    except BaseException:
561	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
562	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
563	        raise
564	    try:
565	        _fsync_directory(directory)
566	    except BaseException as first:
567	        _rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
568	        raise

603	def _replay(
604	    plans: dict[str, dict[str, dict[str, Any]]],
605	    idempotency: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
606	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
607	    key: str,
608	    request: dict[str, Any],
609	) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], bool] | None:
610	    binding = idempotency.get(key)
611	    if binding is None:
612	        return None
613	    if binding != request:
614	        raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with a "
615	                         "different request")
616	    # An equivalent replay returns the current record without writing;
617	    # the committed audit snapshot names the plan the key first served.
618	    result = events[key]["result"]
619	    current = plans[result["job_id"]][str(result["attempt"])]
620	    return copy.deepcopy(current), False

637	def plan(
638	    jobs: str,
639	    supply: str,
640	    trades: str,
641	    dispatch: str,
642	    ledger: str,
643	    job_id: str,
644	    key: str,
645	    owner: str,
646	    source: str | None,
647	    at: int,
648	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
649	    """Create the execution plan for one claimed decision idempotently.
650	
651	    ``jobs``, ``supply``, ``trades``, ``dispatch`` and ``ledger`` paths,
652	    ``job_id``, ``key`` and ``owner`` must be non-empty strings,
653	    ``source`` must be ``None`` or a string (an empty string counts as
654	    no source) and ``at`` a non-boolean non-negative integer moment; the
655	    five paths must also resolve to distinct real locations. Any
656	    violation raises ``ValueError`` before a business file is read.
657	
658	    The ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file, the resource supply file, the
659	    ``market.clear`` clearing ledger and the dispatch ledger are read as
660	    one snapshot under their shared locks together with the execution
661	    ledger's exclusive lock, all five taken in resolved real-path order
662	    so concurrent calls can never deadlock. Only a ``claimed`` decision
663	    held by ``owner`` and still inside its lease is accepted: a decision
664	    in any other state raises ``ValueError``, a different owner raises
665	    ``PermissionError`` and a moment past the lease end raises
666	    ``TimeoutError``. The plan is numbered by the decision's dispatch
667	    attempt count and fixes the job, the traded resource id and version,
668	    the deadline, the owner and the lease end; one dispatch attempt
669	    yields at most one plan.
670	
671	    An empty ``source`` creates a ``launch`` plan (steps ``stage`` then
672	    ``start``). A non-empty ``source`` creates a ``migrate`` plan (steps
673	    ``copy`` then ``switch``): the source must name a published resource
674	    other than the target whose residency list covers the job's
675	    residency regions, else ``LookupError``. A job without a recorded
676	    trade raises ``LookupError`` as well, and an unknown job or decision
677	    raises ``KeyError``.
678	
679	    Returns ``(plan, created)``. A missing execution ledger is created
680	    only by this call, the plan, its idempotency binding and the audit
681	    event -- the complete request plus the committed plan snapshot -- in
682	    one synced atomic write. Replaying the same key with the same job,
683	    owner, source and moment returns the current plan with ``False``
684	    without rewriting; the same key with a different action, job,
685	    attempt, owner, source, step, result, receipt or moment raises
686	    ``ValueError`` with the ledger untouched.
687	
688	    Missing input files or a missing ledger parent raise
689	    ``FileNotFoundError``; invalid structure, values, ordering,
690	    references or canonical bytes raise ``ValueError``; other locking,
691	    read/write or sync failures raise ``OSError``.
692	    """
693	    for value in (jobs, supply, trades, dispatch, ledger, job_id, key,
694	                  owner):
695	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
696	            raise ValueError("jobs, supply, trades, dispatch, ledger, "
697	                             "job_id, key and owner must be non-empty "
698	                             "strings")
699	    if source is not None and not isinstance(source, str):
700	        raise ValueError("source must be None or a string")
701	    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
702	        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
703	    source = source or None
704	
705	    job_real = os.path.realpath(jobs)
706	    supply_real = os.path.realpath(supply)
707	    trades_real = os.path.realpath(trades)
708	    dispatch_real = os.path.realpath(dispatch)
709	    ledger_real = os.path.realpath(ledger)
710	    business_reals = {job_real, supply_real, trades_real, dispatch_real,
711	                      ledger_real}
712	    if len(business_reals) != 5:
713	        raise ValueError("jobs, supply, trades, dispatch and ledger "
714	                         "paths must be distinct real paths")
715	    # Completion ledgers beside the snapshots complete the trades
716	    # ledger's capacity envelope; discovered before locking and shared
717	    # in the global order, so a concurrent completion cannot deadlock.
718	    completion_reals = set(
719	        _market._discover_completion_paths(tuple(sorted(business_reals))))
720	
721	    store = _get_store(ledger)
722	    with store.lock:
723	        # Locks are taken in one resolved-real-path order shared by
724	        # every caller, so concurrent plans can never deadlock; the
725	        # execution ledger lock is exclusive, the input snapshots shared.
726	        with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
727	            for locked in sorted(business_reals | completion_reals):
728	                stack.enter_context(
729	                    _lock(locked, shared=(locked != ledger_real)))
730
